title: LINK external std2 vertical spectrum
summary: Delegate sTDA, sTD-DFT, XsTDA or XsTD-DFT spectra to std2 using a converged external ground-state Molden wavefunction.
gates: converged ground-state orbitals supplied by the reference backend at the requested fixed geometry
explicit Molden producer style and compatible AO ordering and normalization
explicit global exchange fraction or supported native RSH preset; no inferred functional mapping
fresh work directory and unchanged input SHA-256
exact authorized launch plan with one process and explicit OpenMP threads
std2 completion marker and finite spectral rows; zero exit status alone is insufficient
excitation energies in eV with 0.0001 eV print precision; no total-energy or gradient capability inferred
native complete state vectors exported for APOC; overlap, phase, ambiguity and root continuity are owned exclusively by APOC
coordinate_policy: Fixed reference geometry and atom ordering from Molden. Across geometries, APOC owns cross-AO overlaps, phase, ambiguity and root continuity; energy ordering never establishes state identity.
backend_policy: External std2 owns the excited-state kernel and response. The original ab-initio ground-state backend owns its energy and gradient. APOC owns root following through the std2 state adapter (restricted and unrestricted spin-conserving states); LINK does not duplicate overlap or matching logic. This protocol produces vertical spectra and native state vectors. FAST_TDA remains the resident XTB-sTDA implementation.
